name: Cruise Packing Checklist
description: A complete cruise packing checklist covering documents, formal and casual attire, cabin essentials, shore-excursion gear and what not to bring.

items.text: Passport or required ID and any visas
Cruise boarding pass and luggage tags
Credit card and some cash for ports
Printed copies of key documents as backup
items.note: Store copies separately from the originals.

items.text: At least one formal outfit per formal night
items.note: Check your cruise line's dress code before you pack.

items.text: Accessories: jewelry, tie, or a clutch
A wrap or light jacket for cool dining rooms
A light sweater for air-conditioned areas
Workout clothes if you plan to use the gym
Small first-aid kit and pain relievers
A power bank and the right charging cables
A magnetic hook or two for the metal cabin walls
A nightlight and a lanyard for your cruise card
Small day pack for off-ship trips
Cash in local currency for ports
Carry-on with day-one essentials for embarkation
Candles or anything with an open flame

items.note: Most lines limit or prohibit bringing your own alcohol.

items.text: Anything on your cruise line's prohibited-items list

faq.q: What should I pack for a cruise?
faq.a: Pack your travel documents, casual daywear, swimwear, at least one formal outfit, comfortable shoes, and toiletries. Add a small carry-on with day-one essentials since checked bags may not reach your cabin for several hours.

faq.q: What should I wear on formal night?
faq.a: Most lines suggest cocktail or semi-formal attire, such as a dress or a suit, for formal evenings. Check your cruise line's dress code in advance and pack at least one dressier outfit per formal night listed on your itinerary.

faq.q: What can't you bring on a cruise?
faq.a: Cruise lines typically ban irons, candles, drones, and large amounts of alcohol, and they restrict power strips with surge protectors. Review your line's prohibited-items list before you pack to avoid having things confiscated at the terminal.

faq.q: Can I print this cruise packing checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off each item as you pack and again when you disembark.

faq.q: Do I need a carry-on for embarkation day?
faq.a: Yes. Pack a small carry-on with medications, swimwear, sunscreen, and a change of clothes because your checked luggage may take several hours to arrive at your cabin after boarding.
